edges.effect_quant: Topical tretinoin has one of the better evidence bases in cosmetic dermatology, with consistent improvements in fine wrinkling, mottled pigmentation, and texture over months of use.
edges.mechanism: Tretinoin binds retinoic-acid receptors in epidermal and dermal cells, normalizes keratinocyte turnover, and stimulates collagen remodeling while suppressing matrix-degrading enzymes. That makes its effect more structural than cosmetic cover-up: the main trade-off is irritation, not lack of biologic plausibility.
edges.summary: If there is a topical gold standard for photoaging, tretinoin is still the one to beat. The literature is not flashy, but it is consistent: randomized trials and later systematic reviews repeatedly show visible improvement in photodamage markers when patients stay on treatment long enough to get past the early irritation phase.
edges.caveats: Tolerability is the main limiter, especially with stronger formulations or frequent use. The benefit is gradual, and comparative studies often show that alternatives can be gentler even when they are not clearly more effective.
